datasets: NIBRS Group A Crime Data (Open Baltimore)
concurrency_primitives: 2 reader goroutines + sync.WaitGroup (analysis.go:57-64); per-dataset parsing worker pool over bounded chan (cap 256) with sync.Mutex error capture (159-215); N hash-partitioned join/aggregate goroutines each owning a bounded shard chan, FNV-32a routing (66-81,105-134); results merged via channel
design_patterns: Pipeline (read -> parse pool -> partitioned aggregate -> merge -> Report); cmd/internal package layout
questions: Which neighborhoods have the most vacancy notices, and how many crime records and distinct cases are reported there?
How concentrated are notices in the top 10/25/50/100% of vacancy neighborhoods, and what share of distinct crime cases occurs there?
What crime types are reported in neighborhoods with versus without notices?
How do monthly crime record counts vary in neighborhoods with notices?
Which neighborhoods rank highest on a transparent combined planning score?
overview: A disciplined Go pipeline split into cmd/baltimore (flags) and internal/analysis (Load/Report). Two streaming CSV readers feed bounded channels into parsing worker pools and hash-partitioned join/aggregation workers that exclusively own their maps, with strict input validation and four tests including a serial-vs-parallel equivalence check. Maintainable and race-clean, though analysis and all report rendering share one 350-line file.
stakeholder_value: A City Planning office would learn that the top 10% of vacancy neighborhoods hold 60% of notices but only 14% of distinct crime cases, and that Carrollton Ridge, Broadway East and Sandtown-Winchester rank highest on a combined vacancy/crime score while Downtown is crime-heavy but vacancy-light. The joins are meaningful per-neighborhood aggregations, not coincidental counting, though Q3/Q4 are unnormalized counts.
issues: README says 'cd data-processing-engine' but no such folder exists in the submission
Join/aggregation and all output formatting live in one file; no separate output package
Q3/Q4 use raw counts without normalizing for group size
fnv.New32a() allocated per event in dispatcher loop
No run script; commands only in README
rationale: Clean build, two verified real bundled datasets, full parallel parse and partitioned join with race-clean deterministic results, documented and evident memory design, and five cross-dataset questions for a named stakeholder earn near-full marks. Small deductions for monolithic analysis file, two shallower questions with a single chart, and a trivial README path mismatch give 95/100 (A).
